stem: RA 9147, the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act, makes killing wildlife illegal, with a few exceptions. Which of these is one of the exceptions in Section 27(a)?
choices: Killing it to sell its meat in a market
Killing it to prevent imminent danger to human life
Killing it because it keeps eating garden crops
Killing it to use its skin as a decoration
answer: Killing it to prevent imminent danger to human life
hints: The exceptions are about religious rituals, sick or suffering animals, human safety and approved research. None is about profit or convenience.
Read the five exceptions listed under Section 27(a), numbered (i) to (v).

Check each choice against the five: tribal religious rituals, an incurable communicable disease, ending the animal's misery, imminent danger to a person, and use in authorized research. Only one choice matches.

solution.methodName: Check the act against the law's list of prohibited acts

steps.action: Recall Section 27(a) of RA 9147: "killing and destroying wildlife species" is illegal, except in five instances.
steps.why: Wildlife means wild plants and animals in all stages of growth, including those in captivity (Section 5(x)).

steps.action: List the five exceptions: (i) religious rituals of established tribal groups or indigenous cultural communities; (ii) the animal has an incurable communicable disease; (iii) to end its misery; (iv) "to prevent an imminent danger to the life or limb of a human being"; and (v) after use in authorized research or experiments.
Check the choices: selling meat, protecting a garden and using the skin for decoration are not on the list. Only preventing danger to human life is.
The answer is killing it to prevent imminent danger to human life.

trapNotes.Killing it to sell its meat in a market: Selling wildlife is not an exception. Trading of wildlife is itself listed as an illegal act in Section 27(e).
trapNotes.Killing it because it keeps eating garde: Protecting a garden is not one of the five exceptions. The danger must be to the life or limb of a person.
trapNotes.Killing it to use its skin as a decorati: This is not an exception. Collecting or possessing wildlife by-products is itself listed as an illegal act in Section 27(f).

sourceRef.citation: RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act), Section 27(a)
